# espalier_network (Resource)

A network of the container runtime (`container network create`). Changing any argument replaces the network. A subnet the runtime chose may change when the runtime restarts; set `subnet` to keep it fixed.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A NAT network whose subnet the runtime chooses (it may change when the
# runtime restarts).
resource "espalier_network" "default" {
  name = "apps"
}

# A host-only network with a fixed subnet.
resource "espalier_network" "internal" {
  name     = "backend"
  internal = true
  subnet   = "192.168.100.0/24"
  labels = {
    owner = "platform"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the network.

### Optional

- `internal` (Boolean) Host-only network without a route off the host (`--internal`). Defaults to `false` (NAT).
- `labels` (Map of String) Labels attached to the network.
- `subnet` (String) IPv4 subnet in CIDR notation. Chosen by the runtime if not set.
- `subnet_v6` (String) IPv6 prefix in CIDR notation. Chosen by the runtime if not set.

### Read-Only

- `gateway` (String) IPv4 gateway address of the network.
- `id` (String) The network's name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Networks are imported by name.
terraform import espalier_network.default apps
```
